stories.title: Coinbase launches fixed-rate BTC-backed USDC loans on Morpho Midnight - the first enterprise-scale deployment of the fixed-rate protocol
stories.summary: Coinbase launched fixed-rate loans powered by Morpho Midnight: USDC borrowing against BTC with the rate and maturity locked at origination, settling on Base via cbBTC. It is the first enterprise-scale integration of Midnight, a protocol designed around defined rates and maturities - the structural missing piece of onchain credit, which until now ran almost entirely on variable rates - and it sits alongside Coinbase's existing $1.4B variable-rate Morpho book. For builders on onchain credit this is proof that open credit infrastructure can be wrapped into a consumer app without rebuilding the stack. Caveat: onchain lending on Base, not a bank loan; secondary reporting says eligibility is limited to U.S. users outside New York.

quality.note: Morpho blog fetched live (22 Sep 2026, confirms fixed-rate USDC-against-BTC launch, first enterprise-scale Midnight integration, $1.4B existing variable book); @CoinDesk post in-window (18:18 UTC 22 Sep); @BitcoinMagazine amplified 21:08:37 UTC 22 Sep. stories.title: PQLN: post-quantum security for Lightning's off-chain surfaces - hybrid ML-DSA/ML-KEM extension implemented in rust-lightning
stories.summary: East Texas A&M researchers published PQLN (arXiv 2609.13781, 12 Sep): a hybrid post-quantum extension of Lightning that protects the off-chain surfaces a post-quantum Bitcoin consensus upgrade would miss - gossip, peer transport, invoices, payment onions and offers - with ML-DSA/ML-KEM, fitting the larger post-quantum material into Lightning's existing message sizes and verified interoperable with unmodified nodes in a rust-lightning fork. Measured cost: at most 0.33 ms of extra crypto work; the real cost is bandwidth, with gossip growing ~10x under ML-DSA. For builders on quantum-readiness this is the first end-to-end PQ design, implementation and evaluation for Lightning, killing harvest-now-decrypt-later on the payment channel network. Caveat: it is a preprint with a research fork, not a network upgrade - and it does not protect on-chain channel funds.

quality.note: arXiv abstract fetched live (submitted 12 Sep 2026; confirms hybrid ML-DSA/ML-KEM, all off-chain surfaces, 0.33 ms added ops, ~10x gossip with ML-DSA, rust-lightning interop evaluation); @BitcoinMagazine post in-window (19:03:12 UTC 22 Sep). stories.title: NIH highlights oveporexton (Orzeyful) - the first orexin-restoring NT1 drug, a mechanism class the agency's own basic research enabled
stories.summary: NIH posted a recap of oveporexton (Orzeyful, Takeda), FDA-approved 5 Aug 2026 as the first narcolepsy-type-1 therapy that restores missing orexin signaling rather than masking wakefulness symptoms - a mechanism enabled by NIH-funded basic science on the orexin system. For builders on sleep/aging intersection this is the template that matters: a first-in-class mechanism approved for a core sleep disorder in a population with strong metabolic-aging overlap, with DEA scheduling still pending per secondary sources. Caveat: the approval was 5 Aug 2026 - the in-window item is NIH's 22 Sep post, a recap, not new regulatory action.

quality.note: Official @NIH post 19:06:06 UTC 22 Sep, in-window (text highlights oveporexton as first orexin-restoring NT1 therapy); FDA approval announcement (5 Aug 2026) is the underlying primary record. Labeled Catch-up: the approval predates the window, included because the mechanism-class milestone has no dedicated coverage in prior editions.
